items.readable_text:
Content:
The standard algorithm for multiplication works in the same way when multiplying three-digit numbers by three-digit numbers.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's compute [MATH: 237 \times 142.] We start by writing it in the usual way:

Content:
[MATH: 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2|474 + 9, 480 + 23, 700 =]

Content:
First, we multiply the ones:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4|237 × 2 = 4740000000,]

Content:
Next, we multiply the tens. Remember that when multiplying the tens, the result will always end in a zero.

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}2[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4; 9|4|8|0|237 × 40 = 9, 48000000]

Content:
Next, we multiply the hundreds. Since a hundred ([MATH: 100]) has two zeros at the end, the result will end in two zeros! So, we write these first:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}2[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4; 9|4|8|0; 2|3|7|0|0|237 × 100 = 23, 700000]

Content:
Then, we proceed to multiply the rest of the hundreds as usual.

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}2[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4; 9|4|8|0; 2|3|7|0|0|237 × 100 = 23, 700000]

Content:
Finally, we add the results:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}2[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4; +|9|4|8|0; +|2|3|7|0|0; 3|3|6|5|4|474 + 9, 480 + 23, 700 =; = 33, 654]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 237 \times 142 = 33 , 654.]

Finally, we add the results:

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The standard algorithm for multiplication works in the same way when multiplying three-digit numbers by three-digit numbers.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's compute [MATH: 237 \times 142.] We start by writing it in the usual way:

Content:
[MATH: 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2|474 + 9, 480 + 23, 700 =]

Content:
First, we multiply the ones:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4|237 × 2 = 4740000000,]

Content:
Next, we multiply the tens. Remember that when multiplying the tens, the result will always end in a zero.

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}2[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4; 9|4|8|0|237 × 40 = 9, 48000000]

Content:
Next, we multiply the hundreds. Since a hundred ([MATH: 100]) has two zeros at the end, the result will end in two zeros! So, we write these first:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}2[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4; 9|4|8|0; 2|3|7|0|0|237 × 100 = 23, 700000]

Content:
Then, we proceed to multiply the rest of the hundreds as usual.

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}2[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4; 9|4|8|0; 2|3|7|0|0|237 × 100 = 23, 700000]

Content:
Finally, we add the results:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}2[/math]; [math]\color{blue}1[/math]; 2|3|7; ×|0|0|0|1|4|2; 4|7|4; +|9|4|8|0; +|2|3|7|0|0; 3|3|6|5|4|474 + 9, 480 + 23, 700 =; = 33, 654]

Therefore, [MATH: 237 \times 142 = 33 , 654.]
